title: Tonbo Imaging IPO Draws Strong Demand Despite Weaker FY26 Earnings
excerpt: The defence imaging maker's Rs 852 crore offer-for-sale was subscribed 4 times on Day 1 and over 6 times by Day 2 afternoon, with a grey market premium near 71%.
body:
• Tonbo Imaging's Rs 852.18 crore IPO closed Day 1 subscribed 4.00 times — QIB 3.92x, NII 5.95x, retail 3.20x — and reached 6.29 times by early afternoon on Day 2.
  • The price band is Rs 665-700, lot size 21 shares, minimum application Rs 14,700. The issue closes October 19; listing is set for October 23 on BSE and NSE.
  • The issue is entirely an offer for sale of 1.22 crore shares: no IPO money goes to the company. Anchor investors put in Rs 255.36 crore on October 14.
  • Grey market premium is around Rs 500, roughly 71% over the top of the band — against FY26 revenue down 22.7% and profit down about 30%.

Investors are bidding aggressively for a defence technology company whose earnings fell last year. The initial public offering of Bengaluru-based Tonbo Imaging India was subscribed 4.00 times at the close of Day 1 on October 15, and demand kept building on Day 2, reaching 6.29 times by 1:30 pm on October 16 on BSE data, Inc42 reports. The grey market premium has risen to about Rs 500 a share, roughly 71% above the Rs 700 top of the price band, implying an estimated listing price near Rs 1,200.

The subscription picture

Day 1 demand was broad-based rather than retail-only. Non-institutional investors subscribed 5.95 times, qualified institutional buyers 3.92 times excluding the anchor portion, and retail investors 3.20 times, with about 5.40 lakh applications and bids for roughly 3.41 crore shares against about 85.26 lakh shares on offer to the public, according to Univest's subscription tracker. Within the NII category, smaller bidders subscribed 8.72 times and the employee category reached 6.49 times. Ahead of the open, the company allotted 36,48,013 shares to 43 anchor investors at Rs 700, raising Rs 255.36 crore. The public offer reserves 50% for QIBs, 15% for NIIs and 35% for retail investors.

What the company does

Founded in 2003, Tonbo designs electro-optical and infrared systems — thermal imaging cores, weapon sights, targeting and fire-control systems and missile seekers — and says it has deployed more than 28,000 systems across 24 countries. Its red herring prospectus cites a Frost & Sullivan estimate that it supplied about 51% of thermal imaging units bought by the Indian government between April 2024 and March 2026. Growth options include a missile seeker programme with Bharat Dynamics, where it is the sole-source supplier for an uncooled seeker, and high-power microwave systems to counter drone swarms — though management indicates deliveries from those opportunities are expected only in FY29-FY30.

"Defence businesses need to be looked at over a three-to-five-year window."

— Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar, CEO, Tonbo Imaging

The valuation question

The financials are the counterweight to the demand. Revenue from operations fell 22.7% in FY26 to Rs 362.65 crore, net profit fell about 30% to Rs 50.88 crore, and the company recorded a net loss of Rs 17.74 crore in the June 2026 quarter. Management attributes the FY26 decline to international programmes that slipped into FY27 rather than lost business. The order book stood at Rs 314.24 crore at June 30, 2026, about 87% of FY26 revenue. At the top of the band the company is valued at roughly Rs 4,010 crore — about 79 times FY26 profit. Because the issue is a pure offer for sale by existing shareholders, none of the Rs 852.18 crore raised strengthens the company's balance sheet.

What happens next

Bidding closes Monday, October 19. Allotment is expected to be finalised on October 21, with listing on BSE and NSE scheduled for October 23. Grey market premiums are unofficial and unregulated, and the subscription multiple will move before the close; the figures that decide the investment case are the final category-wise subscription, the listing price against the Rs 700 issue price, and whether the delayed international programmes convert into FY27 revenue.
